panel:input: Your guitar's signal as it arrives from the audio interface. Pick the interface and channel your guitar is plugged into, and set how hot it hits the rig.
panel:master: Final output level. A limiter holds peaks at -1 dBFS, so turning this up never hard-clips.
panel:gate: Noise gate: silences hiss and hum between notes. The dot lights while the gate is open.
panel:pitch: Retunes the whole guitar up or down, so you can play songs in other tunings without retuning the strings.
panel:amp: The amplifier: Leviathan's own three-channel amp, a NAM capture of a real amp, or your own capture.
panel:cab: The speaker cabinet and microphone, as an impulse response (IR). This shapes the tone more than anything except the amp.
panel:eq: 8-band graphic EQ after the cabinet, for final tone shaping. Drag a fader; double-click for 0.
panel:delay: Echo. Sync it to the tempo with a note length, or set the time in milliseconds.
panel:reverb: Room ambience after everything else, in stereo. Smooth and natural on clean tones; keep the Mix low on heavy rhythm parts.
panel:pedals: Effects before the amp, in signal order from left to right. Drag to reorder; + Add pedal for more.
inGain: Boost or cut your guitar before the rig. More gain means more distortion from the amp. Set the interface's own gain so it never clips first.
inputDevice: The audio interface your guitar is plugged into.
inputChannel: Which input on the interface your guitar is plugged into.
masterVol: Overall output level of the rig.
gateThresh: How quiet the signal must get before the gate closes. Raise it (toward -20 dB) if hiss gets through; lower it if note tails get cut off.
gateRelease: How quickly the gate closes once you stop playing. Short (under 100 ms) is tight for chugs; long (up to 2 s) lets held notes and feedback fade out naturally. Hold Shift while dragging for fine steps.
gateDepth: How far the gate turns things down when it closes. Full silences the gaps; less (toward 0 dB) only softens them, which sounds more natural on clean and crunch tones.
pitchSemis: Shift in semitones: -2 turns E standard into D standard, -5 into B standard.
pitchCents: Fine tuning in cents (1/100 of a semitone), to match a recording that's slightly off concert pitch.
pitchMix: Blend of shifted and original sound. 100% is a pure retune; lower values give an octave or harmony effect.
ampGain: Preamp drive: from clean to heavily distorted.
bass: Low end (around 100 Hz). Too much makes palm mutes flubby.
mid: Midrange (around 600 Hz–1 kHz). Cutting it scoops the tone; boosting it helps you cut through a band mix.
treble: High end (around 3 kHz). Adds bite and pick attack.
presence: Upper treble from the power amp (around 4–6 kHz). Adds air and sizzle; too much sounds fizzy.
depth: Low-end resonance from the power amp (around 80 Hz). Adds thump to palm mutes.
namInput: How hard you hit the captured amp. More input means more distortion, like turning up the gain.
namOutput: The captured amp's output level. Captures are already level-matched; use this to balance presets.
capDrive: How hard you hit your own capture.
cabMic: Where the microphone sits: centre of the speaker is brighter and tighter, edge is darker and rounder.
irBlend: Blend of the two microphones: 0% is all mic A, 100% is all mic B.
cabLowCut: Removes rumble below this frequency. 80–120 Hz tightens high-gain tones.
cabHighCut: Removes fizz above this frequency. 7–10 kHz tames harsh distortion.
delayFeedback: How many echoes: low for a single slapback, high for long trails.
delayTone: Brightness of the echoes. Darker echoes sit behind your playing.
delayMix: How loud the echoes are compared with your playing.
revSize: How long the reverb rings: from a small room (about a third of a second) to a big hall (about five seconds). Bigger rooms also sound darker.
revMix: How much reverb is mixed in.
panel:doubler: Doubler: makes one guitar sound like two takes panned left and right, the way records are made. Your playing stays in the centre with no added delay, and it sounds the same on a mono speaker.
doublerWidth: How wide the doubled sound spreads. 0% is a single guitar in the middle; higher sounds like two guitars, left and right.
doublerTime: How far apart the two takes are. Shorter sounds tight and glossy, longer sounds like two separate players.
compSustain: How much the compressor evens out your playing. More sustain makes notes ring longer and quiet notes louder.
compAttack: How quickly the compressor reacts. Slower lets the pick attack through.
compBlend: Mix of compressed and dry signal (parallel compression).
wahPos: Wah pedal position: heel down (dark) to toe down (bright). Map an expression pedal to it with MIDI.
wahSens: Auto-wah: how much your picking opens the wah.
wahQ: How sharp and vocal the wah sounds.
odDrive: Overdrive amount. In front of a high-gain amp, keep it low and the level high to tighten the low end.
odLevel: The overdrive's output level; how hard it pushes the amp.
chorusDepth: How much the chorus wobbles the pitch.
chorusMix: Blend of chorus and dry sound.
flangerFb: Flanger resonance: more feedback sounds more metallic, like a jet plane.
flangerMix: Blend of flanger and dry sound.
phaserFb: Phaser resonance: higher is more pronounced and vocal.
tremShape: Tremolo waveform: smooth sine to choppy square.
eq0: 80 Hz: low-end thump and weight. Cut if palm mutes get boomy.
eq1: 160 Hz: body and warmth. Too much sounds boomy.
eq2: 320 Hz: low mids. Cutting here clears mud from high-gain tones.
eq3: 640 Hz: midrange body. Cutting it gives a scooped sound; boosting fills it out.
eq4: 1.2 kHz: the core midrange where a guitar cuts through a band. Too much sounds honky or nasal.
eq5: 2.5 kHz: pick attack and bite. Too much sounds harsh.
eq6: 5 kHz: edge and fizz from the distortion. Cut to smooth out a harsh tone.
eq7: 10 kHz: air and sparkle. Mostly hiss in high-gain tones; cut it to darken.
top:meters: Input level (your guitar, after Input gain) and output level. Keep the input out of the red on your interface.
top:latency: Estimated round trip from your strings to your ears. Under 10 ms feels instant; above 15 ms is orange. Hover for the breakdown.
top:rec: Records your dry guitar and the processed sound side by side, with the rig settings, so you can re-amp later (Cmd/Ctrl+R).
top:metro: Metronome on or off. The beat lights show the bar; volume and beats per bar are under the tempo.
top:tempo: Tempo in BPM, for the metronome and synced delay. Click to type a tempo or change the metronome; follows MIDI clock.
top:tap: Tap along with the beat to set the tempo.
top:tuner: Shows the tuner (T). Mutes the output while tuning unless you turn that off.
top:midi: MIDI learn: click this, then a knob or switch, then move a control on your MIDI device to assign it.
top:preset: The current preset. A dot means it has unsaved changes. Click to choose another preset.
top:undo: Undo the last change to the rig: a knob, a switch, a pedal or loading a preset. Press again to go further back.
top:save: Saves your changes into this preset (Cmd/Ctrl+S).
top:saveAs: Saves the current sound as a new preset, leaving this one unchanged (Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+S).
top:recWave: The take being recorded so far.
bladeDrive: Gain of the distortion stage: from crunchy overdrive to heavy, saturated distortion.
bladeLow: Active low shelf (around 180 Hz), up to ±12 dB. Cut for tight palm mutes, boost for weight.
bladeMid: Active midrange, up to ±12 dB, at the frequency set by the Mid shift switch. Boost to cut through a mix.
bladeHigh: Active high shelf (around 2.8 kHz), up to ±12 dB. Adds or tames bite and fizz.
bladeBoost: How much the Boost adds when it's switched on, up to +20 dB of mid-focused gain into the distortion.
bladeBoostOn: Switches the front-end mid boost on: more gain and a tighter, mid-forward attack, like a boost pedal in front.
bladeShift: Moves the Mid control: 650 Hz for body and growl, 1.5 kHz for presence and cut.
bladeDiode: Clipping: MOSFET is smooth and open; Off uses no diodes, for the most headroom and least compression; Silicon is tight, compressed and saturated.
outputDevice: Where you hear Leviathan: your audio interface's output (fastest), the Mac's or PC's headphones, or speakers. Bluetooth and monitor speakers add delay (marked ⚠︎).
settings:buffer: Audio is worked on in blocks of this many samples. Smaller blocks mean less delay but more work for your computer: pick the smallest that never crackles. Each choice shows the delay you'd get.
settings:latency: Time from plucking a string to hearing it: your interface's input, Leviathan's buffers and the output device. Most of it is usually the output device: wired headphones or your interface's own output are fastest; Bluetooth, monitor speakers and EQ apps are slowest.
settings:engine: How much of each buffer's time the sound engine needs at its busiest, and how often audio arrived too late (a dropout, heard as a click). If dropouts climb, choose a bigger buffer.
settings:a4: The tuner's reference pitch. 440 Hz is standard; some bands tune to 432 or 442.
settings:tuning: How your guitar is tuned. The tuner names strings from it, and the Pitch panel offers tunings to play as.
settings:midiDevices: MIDI controllers and pedals Leviathan can hear. Plug one in and it appears here.
settings:midiLast: The latest message from your MIDI device. Move a control to check it's connected.
settings:programChange: Program 1, 2, 3… from your MIDI device loads the 1st, 2nd, 3rd… preset in the Presets list.
settings:midiAssign: Click Learn, click a knob or ON/OFF switch on the rig, then move a control on your MIDI device. An expression pedal on Wah Position makes a real wah.
settings:recordings: Your takes, each with the dry guitar and the sound you heard. Import adds WAV files from elsewhere so you can re-amp them.
settings:nam: Neural Amp Modeler captures of real amps and pedals. Add .nam files and they appear in the Amp panel under Real amps. Free captures at tone3000.com.
settings:cabIRs: Impulse responses of real speaker cabinets. Add WAV files or folders and pick them in the Cabinet panel. Free packs at tone3000.com.
settings:captures: Amp captures made with Leviathan's own capture tool, from the folder shown.
settings:godsCab: The God's Cab impulse-response pack, if you have it, for the Cabinet panel's multi-mic option.
settings:accent: The colour of knobs, switches and highlights. Follow amp channel changes it with the amp's channel.
settings:zoom: Makes everything in the window bigger or smaller.
settings:explain: Shows what the control under the pointer does, in a strip at the bottom of the window (like this one).
settings:version: The version you're running. Leviathan checks GitHub for a newer one; updating downloads it, checks it and reopens Leviathan.
settings:autoUpdate: Checks for a new version each time Leviathan opens, then every few hours. Nothing is installed until you choose Update.
settings:feedback: Opens a form on GitHub (a free account is needed) with your Leviathan version, system version and audio devices filled in. You can see and change everything before you submit.
settings:license: You're free to use, share and change Leviathan. Anything made from it must also be open source under the AGPLv3 and keep the credit “Leviathan by Shane O'Reilly”.
